taxonomy.subtopic: Plasma-cell-rich endarteritis caused by Treponema pallidum

questions.stem_html:
A 27-year-old man presents with a solitary painless penile ulcer and rubbery, nontender inguinal lymph nodes. Dark-field examination of ulcer fluid reveals thin motile spirochetes. The lesion resolves without treatment, but serologic testing is positive.

Which histopathologic process is most characteristic of this lesion?

options.text_html: Neutrophilic microabscesses surrounding intracellular gram-negative diplococci
Plasma-cell-rich inflammation with endothelial swelling and obliterative endarteritis
Multinucleated giant cells with ground-glass nuclear inclusions

questions.explanation_html: T pallidum stimulates a plasma-cell-predominant inflammatory response and proliferative endarteritis, producing ischemic tissue injury in lesions at multiple stages of syphilis. Primary syphilis classically produces a painless chancre with plasma cells and obliterative endarteritis.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Caseating granulomas with acid-fast organisms indicate tuberculosis.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: This pattern is more consistent with gonococcal infection and does not produce a painless chancre.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Herpes infection produces painful grouped vesicles or ulcers and viral cytopathic changes.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Desmoglein autoantibodies cause pemphigus vulgaris, not an infectious genital ulcer.

questions.educational_objective: Recognize the painless primary chancre and connect syphilitic tissue injury to plasma-cell-rich inflammation and obliterative endarteritis.
